title: The Brown adjoint of $Rf_!$ on the localizing category

proof.text: Put $\mathcal C=\mathcal T_X$, $\mathcal D=\mathcal T_Y$. Since $Y$ is separated and of finite type over $k$, [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine] makes it qcqs. For each chosen $c=(j,p)$, [det-sf-comp-coherence-single] gives an exact, direct-sum-preserving restriction $F_c=Rp_*D(j_!):\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$. The source Brown structures and compact generators are assumed; [sk-lem-brown-hypotheses] at $Y$ supplies a locally small triangulated target with direct sums. All sums use the fixed indexing universe.

Apply [lem-pc-brown-representability-right-adjoint] to $F_c$: step 1 gives exactness and preservation of the required sums, and $\mathcal C$ is compactly generated. Obtain $F_c\dashv G_c$, with counit $\varepsilon^c$. Set $f_c^!=G_c$; the natural adjunction bijections give clause (1).

For $F_c\dashv G_c$, [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-shift-compatibility-unique] (iii) equips $G_c$ with coherent integer-shift isomorphisms compatible with both unit and counit. Its uniqueness clause identifies these as the adjunction-induced shifts.
Apply [lem-sf-triangulated-right-adjoint] to step 1 and the compatible shifts of step 3. It makes $G_c$ exact with those shifts, proving clause (2).

For another right adjoint $J$ of $F_c$, [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] gives the unique counit-compatible isomorphism $\gamma:G_c\cong J$. For $a:M\to G_cN$, its $J$-transpose after $\gamma_N$ is $\varepsilon^J_N F_c(\gamma_N a)=\varepsilon^c_N F_c(a)$. Thus this is precisely compatibility with all adjunction bijections, proving the first assertion of clause (3).

source.place: Part (3): uniqueness for a fixed compactification

proof.text: [det-sf-comp-coherence-cocycle] supplies canonical $\phi_{21}:F_1\cong F_2$ with identity and cocycle laws. Apply [lem-trf-adjoint-mate] (all four functors are exact by steps 1 and 4) to obtain adjunction-compatible $\gamma_{21}:G_1\cong G_2$. Its formula is exactly the conjugate $(\phi_{21}^{-1})^c$ of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. The counit identity reads $\varepsilon^2_N F_2(\gamma_{21,N})=\varepsilon^1_N\phi_{21,G_1N}^{-1}$; it fixes each component uniquely by the $F_2\dashv G_2$ bijection.

Conjugation preserves identities and reverses composition by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. Hence $\gamma_{32}\gamma_{21}=(\phi_{21}^{-1}\phi_{32}^{-1})^c=(\phi_{31}^{-1})^c=\gamma_{31}$, and $\gamma_{cc}=1$. These are the required compactification-independence identifications and laws.
